# Superfloat

> Superfloat is an AI hardware company that designs number formats for AI and the chips that compute in them. Its formats, SF4 to SF16, store each value as a sign bit and a scalable value field with no exponent field, so every multiply-add runs without exponent hardware. Its accelerator, Atreides, is built around those formats. Founded in 2024 by Alosh Denny. Website: https://superfloat.si

Superfloat is not related to seaplane floats, fishing floats or swimming floats that share the name.

Key facts:

- Superfloat (SFx) is a family of number formats from 4 to 16 bits for neural-network weights and activations. An SFx value is a sign bit and x-1 fraction bits, the same as Q1.(x-1) signed fixed point: SF16 is Q1.15, with every value strictly between -1 and 1. Trained networks keep almost every weight in a narrow band of values, so the range an exponent buys goes unused; Superfloat drops it.
- Compared with BF16 (8 exponent bits) and FP8 (4 or 5 exponent bits), Superfloat spends no bits on an exponent. Superfloat's target is twice the speed at half the price for the same multiply-accumulate.
- Atreides is Superfloat's AI accelerator. Three chips are signed off on SkyWater's 130 nm process; the first SF16 chip tapes out on ChipFoundry's CI2612 shuttle on 7 December 2026, with parts back in May 2027. A 2 nm (TSMC N2) test chip and an 800 mm² production die are planned for 2027.
- The software is free: the formats, the LLVM compiler, CUDA and C kernels and the Python package `sf` are developed in the open on GitHub as the OpenSilicon Project, kickstarted by Alosh Denny with TinkerHub Foundation.
- Team: Alosh Denny (Founder and CEO), Poojith Devan (Director of R&D), Karthik Prakash (Director of Compiler Design).
- Superfloat began in 2024 as a college major project on quantization (Weight-Aware Selective Quantization).

## Pages

- [Home](https://superfloat.si/): the number format, the compute lab (SF16 vs BF16 multiply-accumulate and systolic arrays), applications and the current raise
- [About](https://superfloat.si/about/): story, vision, mission, team, financial model, the OpenSilicon Project and FAQ
- [Research notes](https://superfloat.si/blogs/): technical notes
- [Inside the Superfloat compute model](https://superfloat.si/blogs/accelerated-hardware/): bit layouts, storage arithmetic, the nine-stage MAC pipeline and the systolic array
- [What is the Superfloat number format?](https://superfloat.si/blogs/superfloat-number-format/): the SFx definition, the SF4 to SF16 range table, comparison with FP16, BF16 and FP8, and measured accuracy
- [Atreides: an AI accelerator with no exponent hardware](https://superfloat.si/blogs/atreides-accelerator/): chip configuration, the FMA unit, Sky130 hardening results against IEEE FP16 and FP32, and the ISA
- [The OpenSilicon Project](https://superfloat.si/blogs/opensilicon-project/): the open-source repositories, the sf Python library and integer-only inference on the Arduino UNO Q
- [Investors](https://superfloat.si/investors/): rounds from pre-seed to production, and how diligence works

## Docs and code

- [Superfloat Python docs](https://docs.superfloat.si/): install, quickstart, concepts, API reference
- [superfloat](https://github.com/aloshdenny/superfloat): the format definition, benchmarks and measured results
- [superfloat.gpu](https://github.com/aloshdenny/superfloat.gpu): Atreides, the Q1.15 accelerator RTL, ISA and Sky130 hardening
- [superfloat.python](https://github.com/aloshdenny/superfloat.python): Python DSL and kernels
- [superfloat.llvm](https://github.com/aloshdenny/superfloat.llvm): compiler
- [superfloat.cuda](https://github.com/aloshdenny/superfloat.cuda): CUDA and C kernels
- [superfloat.arduino](https://github.com/aloshdenny/superfloat.arduino): integer-only inference on the Arduino UNO Q
